scenario: AITA for dumping food on my girlfriends plate at a wedding until it was overflowing? | Me and my girlfriend are moderately overweight. We have been noticing that we were getting fatter still, so I pushed us to try and lose some weight. We now go on walks everyday, we cut the sugar and generally try to eat better and in reasonable quantities. This is being tougher on her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I'm mainly the one trying to keep us on track and very often I have to call her out when she's sliding back into our old eating habits. So this last weekend we went to a wedding together as guests. We were sitting next to each other, together with family members from both our families, all in the same table. Every table had its own food so everyone could just serve themselves. So what happened next was I had to watch as my girlfriend filled her plate up with all kinds of delicious food. I kinda gave her a look like that, but she just shrugged it off as if to say "yeah I know, but we're at a wedding". I was slightly annoyed with her behavior but sort of forgot about it and tried to just enjoy everyone's companies. Some time after that, when she was finished, she was out for more. She asked me to pass her this big plate of shrimp rice so that she could try some of that. That really struck me, but I didn't want to argue right there and then, so what I did was get the srino rice and proceed to fill her plate up until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She just kind of stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me at this point and I thought it was better I just went outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line and they I came off as a controlling jerk. So, am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregard for our agreed upon diet?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My girlfriend and I are both moderately overweight, and we've noticed we're getting even heavier. So, we decided to try losing some weight. We started going on daily walks, cutting out sugar, and trying to eat better and in reasonable quantities. It's been tough, especially for her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I've been the one trying to keep us on track, and I often have to call her out when she's slipping back into our old eating habits. Last weekend, we went to a wedding together. We were sitting next to each other with family members from both our families at the same table. Each table had its own food, so everyone could serve themselves. What happened next was that I watched my girlfriend fill her plate with all kinds of delicious food. I gave her a look, like maybe she should be careful, but she just shrugged it off, as if to say, "Yeah, I know, but we're at a wedding." I was slightly annoyed but tried to enjoy everyone's company. Later, when she was finished, she asked me to pass her this big plate of shrimp rice so she could try some of that. That really bothered me, but I didn't want to argue right there, so instead, I took the shrimp rice and proceeded to fill her plate until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She just kind of stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me, and I thought it was better to go outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line, and that I came off as a controlling jerk. So, am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregarding our agreed-upon diet? Hmm, okay, so I need to think about this. Let's break it down. First, we have a mutual goal to lose weight, and we've agreed on certain steps to achieve that. I'm trying to help her stick to the plan, which is good. But the way I handled the situation at the wedding might not have been the best. I gave her a look when she was filling her plate, which was a non-verbal way of reminding her about our diet. She responded by shrugging it off, indicating she was aware but choosing to eat anyway. Then, when she asked for more food, I reacted by overfilling her plate, which was probably meant to be a way of showing her the consequences of overeating. But instead, it came off as controlling and humiliating. I need to consider the context. We were at a wedding with family members from both sides. It's a social event, and people are more relaxed. My girlfriend might have felt that it was okay to indulge a bit, given the setting. My reaction, however, was to take a stand against her behavior, but the way I did it was public and potentially embarrassing for her. I also need to think about the impact of my actions. By overfilling her plate, I made her feel humiliated, which led her to leave the table. This not only affected our relationship but also drew unwanted attention from others at the table. It's important to communicate concerns privately rather than in public settings to avoid embarrassment. Moreover, controlling behavior, even with good intentions, can be seen as manipulative. My girlfriend felt that I was stepping out of line by trying to control her actions in such a public manner. It's crucial to respect her autonomy and find a more constructive way to address her eating habits. Perhaps a better approach would have been to talk to her privately after the meal or find a way to gently remind her of our goals without making her feel guilty or controlled. It's also important to acknowledge that social events are opportunities to enjoy oneself, and it's okay to have occasional indulgences as part of a balanced approach to dieting. In summary, while my intention was to help her stick to our diet, the method I used was inappropriate and hurtful. It's essential to communicate concerns respectfully and find a balance between maintaining our health goals and respecting each other's autonomy.
